results.claim: DBFT stands for Democratic Byzantine Fault Tolerant consensus.
results.quote: Democratic Byzantine Fault Tolerant (DBFT) consensus

results.claim: DBFT is how the nodes reach consensus on the next block, and it is leaderless.
results.quote: As a leaderless consensus algorithm, it eliminates single points of failure
on: How Redbelly’s nodes agree on the next block, with no leader.

results.claim: In classical blockchains nodes compete; one block wins and the rest is wasted.
results.quote: In classical blockchains, participants solve consensus by having different participants engage in ‘fierce’ competition: proposing their own block and trying to impose it on the system. If they succeed, then all other participants lose: their block is the only one appended at the next available index of the chain. This is a waste of resources as only one participant succeeds and the rest fail.
on: One block wins. The rest is wasted.

results.claim: DBFT nodes cooperate: their transactions are combined into one superblock.
results.quote: Redbelly nodes, on the other hand, solve consensus by combining distinct sets of transactions into a ‘superblock’ in a leaderless manner

results.claim: Redbelly consensus is collaborative instead of competitive.
results.quote: Redbelly consensus is collaborative instead of competitive

results.claim: No leader: every node plays a similar role.
results.quote: each node plays a similar role in the execution of the consensus
on: Every node plays a similar role.

results.claim: No forks: once decided, a block is final.
results.quote: It cannot fork and has been mathematically proven to be correct through a process of formal verification through parameterised model checking

results.claim: Finality is deterministic: a confirmed transaction cannot be reversed.
results.quote: Deterministic finality ensures transactions are confirmed once and cannot be reversed

results.claim: Fault tolerant: proven (by model checking) safe for any number of nodes while fewer than 1 in 3 are faulty.
results.quote: for any number n of processes and any number f < n/3 of Byzantine processes
on: Proven safe if under 1 in 3 nodes are faulty.

results.claim: The proof covers safety (and liveness) for any parameter.
results.quote: we formally verify, for any parameter, not only the safety properties of the Redbelly Blockchain consensus but also its liveness
on: Proven safe if under 1 in 3 nodes are faulty.

results.claim: Proof comes from faulty nodes trying to cause disagreement among honest nodes: they leave signed traces that honest nodes combine into undeniable proofs of fraud.
results.quote: When faulty nodes try to cause disagreement, they leave cryptographically signed traces that honest nodes can combine to build undeniable proofs of fraud
on: Nodes that try to cause disagreement leave proof.
Their signed messages can name them.

results.claim: The trigger is honest nodes disagreeing on the next block. The system can then, eventually, name the faulty nodes responsible (at least a third of the nodes, n/3).
results.quote: if honest nodes disagree on the next block, the system can eventually output at least n/3 faulty nodes who are responsible for the disagreement
on: Their signed messages can name them.

results.claim: Disagreement is only possible with 1 in 3 or more faulty nodes: below that, DBFT is proven safe.
results.quote: for any number n of processes and any number f < n/3 of Byzantine processes
on: Only if 1 in 3 or more nodes are faulty.

results.claim: Consensus like DBFT tolerates fewer than a third of faulty nodes; past that, disagreement becomes possible.
results.quote: Typically, BFT systems can only tolerate less than a third of faulty nodes
on: Only if 1 in 3 or more nodes are faulty.

results.claim: With more than 1 in 3 of the computing power, an attacker can force disagreement; Polygraph, the accountable consensus behind these proofs, exists for this case.
results.quote: If the adversary controls more than 1/3 of the computing power, it can always force disagreement. In this paper, we propose Polygraph, the first accountable Byzantine agreement solution.
on: Only if 1 in 3 or more nodes are faulty.

results.claim: Once honest nodes have enough proofs of fraud, a membership change removes the faulty nodes from the consensus committee.
results.quote: Once honest nodes gather enough proofs of fraud against faulty nodes, they initiate a membership change. This process involves an exclusion protocol to remove the identified faulty nodes from the consensus committee
on: Excluded from consensus with enough proof.
